ConocoPhillips rose 1.6% today to $140.10, continuing a sharp climb over the last three days after hitting a low of $134.47 on November 9th. The timing and direction of this move align closely with Trump's statements on November 10th suggesting the Iran conflict would end "fairly soon" — a development that initially pressured oil prices (Brent crude dipped below $90) but appears to have triggered a reversal as investors reassess energy sector valuations. Oil prices have since stabilized around $89–$92 per barrel, and ConocoPhillips has gained roughly 3.9% in two trading days as confidence in near-term geopolitical risk easing has returned.

The broader context here is that energy stocks have been volatile on Iran tensions, but de-escalation hopes — even tentative ones — can flip investor sentiment quickly in this sector. The stock's 6.6% decline over two weeks reflects the uncertainty baked in before these recent comments, and the rebound suggests traders are rotating back into oil exposure on the belief that worst-case scenarios may be receding.
